Save X and Y in immediate operands, split the packed byte in A into two nibbles plus one, and clear the first two of four display positions. Store zero in the third position if the high nibble is zero, otherwise its nibble-plus-one value; store the low nibble plus one in the fourth position. Restore Y for the draw call, then restore X before returning. Nibbles are not validated as decimal digits.

Immediate operand of the LDY at $A526, which restores the screen offset of the price's last digit for the digit drawer at $A7EC, after $A515 used Y for the high digit. $A507 stores it from the Y that $A4B4 ($9B) and $A4BC ($AF) pass; the load holds $FF.
Immediate operand holding the incoming X, patched at $A504 and restored after the draw call before returning.

Branch on the caller’s N and Z flags after loading the selection value: negative goes to the second-option balance check, zero selects message $A90C, and positive calls the balance-subtraction routine with record field 12. The positive path then checks record field 8 for a callback or its default message. Payment and callback effects are separate from this branch.
When stage-record field 8 ($4771,X), loaded at $A53C, is zero, branch to the default message at $A557. Otherwise $A541 stores it into the high operand byte at $A551 of the JSR at $A54F.
Copy stage-record field 7 ($476B,X) into the low operand byte at $A550 of the JSR at $A54F, then clear field 8.

Call the first option's routine for the stage record in $7B, patched by $A541 (high byte, from $4771,X) and $A547 (low byte, from $476B,X). $A54C then clears the high byte, so the routine runs once and a later choice shows the default message at $A557. In this load the payment record (entry $A49B) names $9351, which shows the message at $9358. The load holds JSR $FF00; afterwards $A552 adds 4 to the meter.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $A54F, whose high byte is $A551. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $A541 first stores the high byte from $4771,X, byte 5 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, and skips the call when it is zero; $A547 then stores this byte from $476B,X (byte 4), and $A54C clears $4771,X so the call runs once. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the first option callback patched from record field 8. After a nonzero callback returns, add 4 to the player meter; when that field is zero, select message $A97A and then add 4. Both paths decrement record field 3 and enter the message wait.

For the second option, proceed when the selected player’s high balance byte is nonzero or the low byte compares at least as large as record field 11; otherwise return to input polling. On proceeding, call the balance-subtraction routine with field 11 and inspect record field 10.
When stage-record field 10 ($477D,X), loaded at $A57D, is zero, branch to the default message at $A598. Otherwise $A582 stores it into the high operand byte at $A592 of the JSR at $A590.
Copy stage-record field 9 ($4777,X) into the low operand byte at $A591 of the JSR at $A590, then clear field 10.

Call the second option's routine for the stage record in $7B, patched by $A582 (high byte, from $477D,X) and $A588 (low byte, from $4777,X). $A58D then clears the high byte, so the routine runs once. In this load the payment record (entry $A49B) names $9385, which shows the message at $938C. The load holds JSR $FF00; afterwards $A593 adds 8 to the meter.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $A590, whose high byte is $A592. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $A582 first stores the high byte from $477D,X, byte 7 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, and skips the call when it is zero; $A588 then stores this byte from $4777,X (byte 6), and $A58D clears $477D,X so the call runs once. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the second option callback patched from record field 10. After a nonzero callback returns, add 8 to the player meter; when that field is zero, select message $A995 and then add 8. Both paths decrement record field 3 and enter the message wait.
Initializes a two-choice item interaction, draws options and prices, samples joystick input and invokes the selected record's effect callback.
Patch the low byte of the player-dependent state address.
Patch the high byte of the player-dependent state address.

The address operand is patched by $A5F5 and $A5FC with $4DD5 plus stage-record field 8 plus the selected player index, so field 8 values 0, 2 and 4 read the selected player's byte of the arrays at $4DD5, $4DD7 and $4DD9. The $FF00 in the load is a placeholder.
Low address operand of the LDA at $A5FF, paired with high byte $A601. $A5F5 patches it with the low byte of $4DD5 plus stage-record field 8 plus the selected player index before the read.

High byte of the selected-player state address patched at $A5FC. With decimal mode clear, the following code reads that state, adds the lookup byte indexed by record field 8, and stores the wrapped result as the first item ID; it stores that result plus one as the second item ID. Drawing begins at the separate entry $A60F.
Load the second item ID at $A851, multiply it by eight with three ASLs and put the wrapped offset in Y for the item-record lookup at $A616.
Copy byte 2 of the second item's eight-byte record ($ABA3,Y) into the low operand byte at $A625 of the JSR at $A624.
Copy byte 3 of the second item's eight-byte record ($ABA4,Y) into the high operand byte at $A626 of the JSR at $A624.

Call the draw routine of the second item on offer, with A = $E4, the screen offset to draw at. $A619 and $A61F patch the address from bytes 2 and 3 of the item's eight-byte record ($ABA3,Y and $ABA4,Y, Y = 8 × the item number in $A851). In this load the records name $AB55, an RTS, or one of $AB56, $AB63, $AB68, $AB6D and $AB72, which draw the item's characters. The load holds JSR $FF00.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $A624, whose high byte is $A626. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $A619 stores it from $ABA3,Y and $A61F the high byte from $ABA4,Y, with Y eight times the second item's number $A851: offsets 2 and 3 of its 8-byte item row, the picture routine, called with A=$E4. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the JSR at $A624; the load holds $FF. $A61F stores it from $ABA4,Y and $A619 stores the low byte from $ABA3,Y, with Y eight times the second item's number from $A851, so the call reaches that item's draw routine.
Copy byte 2 of the first item's eight-byte record ($ABA3,Y) into the low operand byte at $A63D of the JSR at $A63C.
Copy byte 3 of the first item's eight-byte record ($ABA4,Y) into the high operand byte at $A63E of the JSR at $A63C.

Call the draw routine of the first item on offer, with A = $D0, the screen offset to draw at. $A631 and $A637 patch the address from bytes 2 and 3 of the item's eight-byte record ($ABA3,Y and $ABA4,Y, Y = 8 × the item number in $A850). In this load the records name $AB55, an RTS, or one of $AB56, $AB63, $AB68, $AB6D and $AB72, which draw the item's characters. The load holds JSR $FF00.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $A63C, whose high byte is $A63E. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $A631 stores it from $ABA3,Y and $A637 the high byte from $ABA4,Y, with Y eight times the first item's number $A850: offsets 2 and 3 of its 8-byte item row, the picture routine, called with A=$D0. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the JSR operand at $A63C, which $A637 patches from byte 3 of the first item's eight-byte record ($ABA4,Y). The call passes A=$D0. After the callback returns, the following code sets up the choice colours and prices.
Set 24 colour cells to 9: two four-column groups, each three rows high, at $D8F8 and $D90C with a 40-byte row stride. The loop counter at $ABA0 ends at zero.

Write $46 plus one to the high address byte at $A800 of the digit store at $A7FE, then call price extraction and drawing for the two item IDs at $A850/$A851. Pass Y=$73 and $87 to the respective drawing calls; then select prompt $A857 in X/Y.

Show the selected prompt, clear the selection index, and set the shared timeout to 220. The first loop waits for held input to be released; each frame decrements the same timeout before updating the HUD and cursor. A timeout before release follows the same timeout path as the later polling loop.

Wait a frame, decrement the shared timeout, then update the HUD and cursor and sample controls. A zero at $70 branches to confirmation, otherwise zero at $73 branches left, otherwise zero at $74 branches right. That order gives confirmation priority over left, and left priority over right. With all three nonzero, poll again.

When the timeout reaches zero, a nonzero layout selector jumps to $A5B5. With selector zero, write $FF to field 3 of the selected stage record and pass message $A88C to $A78B. The destination routines and callback effects are separate from this timeout check.

For left input, return to the release loop without a change when the selection index has its sign bit set. Otherwise decrement it. If the result is nonzero and the layout selector is zero, call the description routine with the first item ID; then update the cursor and return to the release loop.

For right input, return to the release loop without a change when the selection index is exactly 1. Otherwise increment it. If the result is nonzero and the layout selector is zero, call the description routine with the second item ID; then update the cursor and return to the release loop. Values outside the usual $FF, 0 and 1 are not clamped by this code.
If the layout selector is nonzero, pass the selection index in A to the option dispatcher at $A52E. Otherwise inspect the selected item and stage record.

When the selection index is zero, a negative stage-record field 3 or a clear bit 1 selects message $A8B4. A nonnegative field with bit 1 set selects message $A89D. Nonzero selection indexes instead enter the item-price path.

Use the first item ID when the nonzero index has its sign bit set, otherwise the second item ID. Multiply the ID by eight, use it as an offset into the item records, and pass the first two record bytes in $7D/$7E to the balance-subtraction routine.

If balance subtraction returns carry clear, go back to the release loop. On carry set, decrement stage-record field 3, choose the item ID again by the index sign and use its record to patch an item-effect call. With decimal mode clear, pass item ID plus one in A. After the callback returns, select message $A879.
Copy byte 4 of the chosen item's eight-byte record ($ABA5,Y) into the low operand byte at $A785 of the JSR at $A784.
Copy byte 5 of the chosen item's eight-byte record ($ABA6,Y) into the high operand byte at $A786 of the JSR at $A784.

Call the bought item's purchase routine with A = the item number plus one ($A782). $A777 and $A77D patch the address from bytes 4 and 5 of the item's eight-byte record ($ABA5,Y and $ABA6,Y, Y = 8 × the item number). In this load items 0–3 go to $AC79, which stores the motion tier, items 6–10 to $AC82, which stores the armour profile, and the others to $AC61, $AC67, $AC6D, $AC73, $AC8E, $ACAB, $ACB2, $ACB9 or $ACC0. The load holds JSR $FF00.

Low byte of the target of the JSR at $A784, whose high byte is $A786. The load holds $00 here, so the instruction reads JSR $FF00 until it is patched. $A777 stores it from $ABA5,Y and $A77D the high byte from $ABA6,Y, with Y eight times the bought item's number: offsets 4 and 5 of its 8-byte item row, the purchase routine. No other instruction writes it.

High byte of the selected item-effect callback patched at $A77D. After the callback returns, select message $A879 in X/Y. The common entry at $A78B calls the message display routine, then repeatedly waits a frame and calls the HUD update until $4D6B is zero; it then returns. The HUD update's status-panel path at $3719, which runs on alternate calls, decrements $4D6B at $3725.

Return A unchanged unless it equals $13. For $13, inspect bit $10 of the selected player’s flags: return $14 when set, or $13 when clear. The item-pair initializer calls this for each supplied record item.

Call the input sampler, then test $73, $74 and $70. Return carry set if any of the three is zero; return carry clear if all are nonzero. The mapping from physical controls depends on the separate sampler.

Place the selection pointer: add one (after CLC) to the selection index $A84B, which the left and right handlers keep at −1, 0 or 1, and use the result, 0–2, to read the pointer's X position from $A84C. Pass it in X, with frame $82 in Y, to $719E, which sets up the pointer in display slots 4 and 5.
Load X from record index $7B, write $FF to interaction field $4753,X and return, disabling the current item slot through that field.

With decimal mode clear, multiply the item ID in A by eight and add six with eight-bit wrap. Read the two bytes at that offset in the item-record table as a little-endian message pointer, pass its low byte in X and high byte in Y, and jump to the message display routine. Item bounds and display behavior are separate.

Process four price-display bytes from $A848 down to $A845. Leave zero unchanged; for each nonzero byte add $F5 with eight-bit wrap and decimal mode clear. Call the digit writer at $A7FE with successive Y positions, decrementing Y after each call.

Write A through the indexed store instruction at $A7FE; its high address byte at $A800 is patched by the surrounding layout code. Write colour 1 to $D900,Y and return. The colour destination requires I/O to be visible.

Multiply the item ID in A by eight with eight-bit wrap. Split the two packed bytes from the item record into four nibbles, high record byte first, and store each nibble plus one at $A845–$A848. Starting at the first digit, replace consecutive values of 1 with zero until a different value or all four digits have been processed. Nibbles are not checked for valid decimal digits.

Load 1: first of the four price-display digit codes at $A845–$A848. The price formatter at $A807 stores the high nibble of the item record's high price byte plus one here ($A815), and the leading-zero loop at $A832–$A843 replaces it with zero when it is 1, a zero digit. The payment formatter at $A504 clears it ($A50F). $A7EC reads it for drawing ($A7EE), adding $F5 to a nonzero code. $717C also copies it to $D74D, as byte 5 of character $E9 of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8.

Second of the four price-display digit codes at $A845–$A848. The price formatter at $A807 stores the low nibble of the item record's high price byte plus one here ($A81B) and then replaces it with zero when it and the first code are both 1, a leading zero. The payment formatter at $A504 clears it ($A512). $A7EC reads it for drawing.

Third of the four price-display digit codes at $A845–$A848. The payment formatter at $A504 stores the high nibble of its amount plus one here, or zero when that nibble is zero ($A51D). The price formatter at $A807 stores the high nibble of the item record's low price byte plus one ($A829), replaced with zero when it and the two codes before it are all 1. $A7EC reads it for drawing.

Load 1: fourth of the four price-display digit codes at $A845–$A848. The price formatter at $A807 stores the low nibble of the item record's low price byte plus one here ($A82F), replaced with zero when it and the three codes before it are all 1. The payment formatter at $A504 stores the low nibble of its amount plus one ($A523). $A7EC reads it for drawing. $717C also copies it to $D750, as byte 0 of character $EA of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8.

One byte, $5B, between the four price-digit codes at $A845–$A848 and the layout selector at $A84A. The price formatters at $A504 and $A807 and the digit drawer at $A7EC all stop at four bytes, and no instruction in load 1 or the resident part names it. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8, takes it to $D751.

Load 1: the shop routine's layout selector. The payment-screen set-up at $A4A1 stores $46 plus one here ($A4A7), the same value it puts in the high address byte at $A800 of the digit store at $A7FE; the item-shop set-up at $A5C1 stores 0 ($A5C3). When it is nonzero, the timeout at $A6BE goes to $A5B5, which decrements stage field $4753,X and shows the message at $A956 (“If you have no” / “business, Get out!”); a cursor move skips the item description ($A6E1, $A701); and Fire goes to the option dispatcher at $A52E with the selection index in A ($A712). When it is zero, the timeout stores $FF in $4753,X and shows “Closed.” ($A6C6), a cursor move onto an item shows that item's description through $A7DA, and Fire goes to the purchase path at $A71D. $717C also copies it to $D752, as byte 2 of character $EA of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8.
Current item-selection index. Its sign selects between the two choices in the purchase path.

Selection pointer X positions $5F, $B4 and $FF for the selection index −1, 0 and 1, read by $A7CB with X = index + 1. $A683 starts the index at 0, and the left and right handlers ($A6D4, $A6F2) keep it between −1 and 1.

Load 1: $A84F is the shop's selection countdown. After the opening message, $A688 stores $DC (220) here, and the selection loop decrements it at $A68E and $A6A1, once each time round (each pass calls $3C2A); when it reaches zero the shop gives up at $A6BE. $A850 is the first offered item ID. $717C also copies them to $D757–$D758, as characters $EA–$EB of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8.

Load 1: the first offered item ID of the item shop. The set-up at $A5C1 stores it at $A5DC, from stage field $476B,X through the $13/$14 resolver at $A79A when that field is nonzero, and otherwise at $A606, as the player-state byte that stage field $4771,X selects plus the offset at $A852,Y. The shop reads it to draw the item's picture ($A627) and price ($A664), to show its description when the cursor moves onto it ($A6E6), and, when Fire is pressed with the cursor on it, to check its price ($A743) and run its purchase routine ($A76C). Load 1's stage object records name only the payment entry at $A49B, not the item-shop entry at $A49E, so in load 1 none of this runs. $717C also copies it to $D758, as byte 0 of character $EB of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8.
Second offered item ID. When stage-record field 7 is nonzero, $A5E5 stores field 8 here after the $13/$14 resolver at $A79A; otherwise $A60C stores the first ID plus one, with byte wrapping.

Five bytes, $00, $00, $0D, $00, $06, at $A852–$A856, ending where the message at $A857 starts. When stage-record field 7 is zero, $A603 adds the byte indexed by field 8 to the selected player's state byte read at $A5FF to form the first item ID; nothing bounds the index. The eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8, also takes these bytes to $D75A–$D75E.

Load 1, shop message 1: three zero-terminated fields "     Welcome!" / "  May I help you?" / "", followed by control byte $20. The item-shop setup (entry $A49E, JMP $A5C1, which clears $A84A) draws the two item pictures and prices, loads this address in X/Y at $A67A and falls into the $77E0 call at $A67E. The selection loop that follows (220 passes, counted in $A84F) calls $370B on each pass, so the countdown runs while the player chooses. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 32 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 no stage record names the item-shop entry $A49E (JMP $A5C1): the three records’ callbacks are $93BA, $A49B and $073F, so this message is not shown in load 1.

Load 1: $A878 is the control byte $20 of the message at $A857, three zero-terminated glyph lines “     Welcome!” / “  May I help you?” / “”. $A67A loads its address in X/Y and calls $77E0. $77E2 stores the control byte $20 in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 32 of its updates. $717C also copies it to $D780, as byte 0 of character $F0 of the eight-page character copy for visual selector 4, which starts at $A0F8.

Load 1, shop message 2: three zero-terminated fields "" / "     Thank you." / "", followed by control byte $10. After a purchase in the item shop ($7901 has subtracted the row’s price), the purchase routine named by bytes 4–5 of the item row returns to $A787, which loads this address in X/Y. $A78B calls $77E0 and then waits, calling $370B on each pass, until $4D6B is zero, and returns. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 no stage record names the item-shop entry $A49E (JMP $A5C1): the three records’ callbacks are $93BA, $A49B and $073F, so this message is not shown in load 1.

Load 1, shop message 3: three zero-terminated fields "" / "      Closed." / "", followed by control byte $18. When the selection loop times out in the item shop ($A84A zero), $A6C6 stores $FF in the stage field $4753,X, which closes the shop object, and loads this address in X/Y at $A6CD, then jumps to $A78B. $A78B calls $77E0 and then waits, calling $370B on each pass, until $4D6B is zero, and returns. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 24 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 no stage record names the item-shop entry $A49E (JMP $A5C1): the three records’ callbacks are $93BA, $A49B and $073F, so this message is not shown in load 1.

Load 1, shop message 4: three zero-terminated fields "" / " Please come again." / "", followed by control byte $10. When Fire is pressed on the middle position ($A84B zero) in the item shop and bit 1 of the stage field $4753,X is set, $A734 loads this address in X/Y and jumps to $A78B. $A78B calls $77E0 and then waits, calling $370B on each pass, until $4D6B is zero, and returns. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 no stage record names the item-shop entry $A49E (JMP $A5C1): the three records’ callbacks are $93BA, $A49B and $073F, so this message is not shown in load 1.

Tail of the second field of the message at $A89D: the stored text here is "me again." followed by the second and third field terminators and control byte $10. The earlier bytes complete " Please come again."

Load 1, shop message 5: three zero-terminated fields "Oh, he's" / "just browsing." / "", followed by control byte $10. When Fire is pressed on the middle position ($A84B zero) in the item shop and the stage field $4753,X is negative or has bit 1 clear, $A729 loads this address in X/Y and jumps to $A78B. $A78B calls $77E0 and then waits, calling $370B on each pass, until $4D6B is zero, and returns. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 no stage record names the item-shop entry $A49E (JMP $A5C1): the three records’ callbacks are $93BA, $A49B and $073F, so this message is not shown in load 1.

Load 1, shop message 6: three zero-terminated fields "" / "  Cocktail or Beer." / "", followed by control byte $10. The price-shop setup (entry $A49B, JMP $A4A1, which stores $46+1, never zero, in $A84A) reaches $A4EF when the selected player’s gold covers the second price (record byte 9, $4789,X) or its high byte $4DC7 is nonzero; with bit 0 of the stage field $4753,X set, $A4FD loads this address in X/Y and jumps to the $77E0 call at $A67E. The selection loop that follows (220 passes, counted in $A84F) calls $370B on each pass, so the countdown runs while the player chooses. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 the price shop is stage record 2 at $92DB (callback $A49B, state 5, which $479C lowers by 2 on each visit before the call).

Load 1, shop message 7: three zero-terminated fields "You're here again," / "Beer or Cocktail." / "", followed by control byte $10. The price-shop setup (entry $A49B, JMP $A4A1) reaches $A4EF when the selected player’s gold covers the second price (record byte 9, $4789,X) or its high byte $4DC7 is nonzero; with bit 0 of the stage field $4753,X clear, $A4F6 loads this address in X/Y and jumps to the $77E0 call at $A67E. The selection loop that follows (220 passes, counted in $A84F) calls $370B on each pass, so the countdown runs while the player chooses. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 the price shop is stage record 2 at $92DB (callback $A49B, state 5, which $479C lowers by 2 on each visit before the call).

Load 1, shop message 8: three zero-terminated fields "" / " Please come again." / "", followed by control byte $10. In the price shop ($A84A nonzero), Fire on the middle position ($A84B zero) goes from $A712 to $A52E, which branches to $A5AE when the position is zero; $A5AE loads this address in X/Y and jumps to $A78B. $A78B calls $77E0 and then waits, calling $370B on each pass, until $4D6B is zero, and returns. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status. $77E0 copies each stored space ($20) as a blank cell (0). In load 1 the price shop is stage record 2 at $92DB (callback $A49B, state 5, which $479C lowers by 2 on each visit before the call).

Load 1, shop message 9: three zero-terminated fields "" / "  Never come back!" / "", followed by control byte $10.
